title: After the Passover type: God leads by the desert road, not Philistia
english: ON ADORATION AND WORSHIP IN SPIRIT AND TRUTH — BOOK THREE. That it is impossible to escape the death from sin, and the devil’s greed, except through the sanctification that is according to Christ; and that justification is not in law but in Christ. Therefore since the manner of the sacrifice was being carried through very well for those from Israel, and the firstborn of the Egyptians had already perished, and Christ as in a type was driving the destroyer away from those sanctified, then at last, running out from the land of those who ruled them, and hastening to arrive at the one promised to them, they do not run straight into it, but were being carried round as it were by turnings onto the other side of the straight way. For he writes again thus: ‘And when Pharaoh sent the people out, God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, because it was near. For God said: Lest the people repent when they see war, and turn back into Egypt. And God led his people round by the way into the wilderness toward the Red Sea.’
Palladius: What then is the hidden thing even in this?

Cyril: It must be examined thoroughly, if it seems good. For understand that although a road lying straight before them was at hand, and it was possible for those shortening the journey to arrive quickly (for ‘near,’ he says, ‘was the land of the promise’), clearly he was carrying them away by another—the one in a long circuit—the Creator of all things having known beforehand their readiness toward apostasy, and what still bent unrestrainedly toward cowardice of old.
Palladius: The word is not any clearer.

title: Near road is faith in Christ; Law is the long circuit
english: hope that is with God, faith that is in Christ, and the justification according to him, according at least to what has been said wisely by Paul: ‘Near you is the word, in your mouth and in your heart—that is, the word of faith which we proclaim, that if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord, and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved; for with the heart it is believed unto righteousness, and with the mouth it is confessed unto salvation.’ This road then, thus near and contracted, God was not letting those of old step through; but he was devising as it were some circuit not having the straight way—the law in turns of words and in enigmas, having a longer and not untroubled pedagogy—so that, having the things in shadows as a kind of practice of the more perfect, and being catechized beforehand into the mystery, they would not be simply terrified by whatever frights into flight and apostasy from Christ, but having been trained beforehand as it were and learning thoroughly what truly benefits, they would be readier toward desire and eagerness for the truth, and would have love toward God fixed and unshakeable. Through a long and as it were not straight road, then—the worship according to the letter—the law was pedagogue. But Christ is not so. For he showed us the straight and near one—that is, the one through faith—reforging into boldness, and into the need thereafter to play the man against those who stand opposed; and to love most of all to endure hardship for the good, and to set oneself nobly against the devil’s methods, saying perhaps that word in the prophet: ‘Behold the Lord helps me; who will mistreat me?’ And what produces in us such admirable boldness would surely be nothing other than the power from on high—that is, the sharing and communion of the Holy Spirit.
Palladius: I understand what you say, and I admire you for the keenness.

Cyril: And the time of the salvation through Christ the accompanying text would also mark at once. For ‘In the fifth generation,’ it says, ‘the sons of Israel went up from the land of Egypt.’ For we have been redeemed from slavery, and indeed also from toils in vain distractions, and from misery concerning earth and dust (and you understand what I say), according to the evangelical parable, as in a fifth generation, at the fifth time. For ‘The kingdom of the heavens is like a man, a householder, who went out together with early morning to hire workers into his vineyard.’ And this he also said he does around the sixth and the ninth: ‘And around the eleventh, he found others idle, and said to those: Why have you stood here idle the whole day? Go, you also work into my vineyard.’ Observe then how in a fifth generation the last ones are being sent into the vineyard, and in the times that are

title: Fifth time and Passover lamb; pillar of cloud and fire is Christ
english: last, when the Only-begotten became human, and endured the slaughter for the life of all. Therefore also Moses’ law was typifying that the lamb is to be taken from the tenth of the first month, and slaughtered toward evening of the fourteenth of the same month, so that in the same both the fifth time for us, as on the fifth day, and the things at the end of the age, the Savior’s slaughter coming to be through ‘toward evening,’ might be signified.
Palladius: Therefore the whole aim of God-breathed Scripture, as it seems, looks toward the mystery of Christ?

Cyril: Altogether so; for Christ is the end of law and prophets; ‘Since there is no other name under heaven given among humans in which we must be saved.’ For the Savior’s disciple said thus, and the demonstration is near, if we strike upon what follows. ‘Setting out,’ it says, ‘the sons of Israel from Succoth, they encamped in Etham beside the wilderness; and God was leading them, by day in a pillar of cloud, to show them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire; the pillar of fire did not fail by night before all the people.’ Do you see how, when those from Israel had gone out from the Egyptians’ land, God was leading in a pillar of cloud and of fire? And through both Christ was being written.
Palladius: In what way?

Cyril: First, because a pillar and foundation of the truth is unshakeable and altogether unbreakable, and holding the earth up high. For in Christ we have been freed from minding the things of flesh, and from rolling in earthly evils; and we are lifted as it were high through him, minding things above, and citizenshiping in heaven. For it is written that ‘The mighty ones of God of the earth have been raised up exceedingly.’ And Christ also said somewhere through David’s voice concerning both the earth and the holy apostles: ‘I have made firm her pillars.’ For the holy disciples who hold up the earth were made firm, having put on the power from on high—that is, the grace through the Holy Spirit. And they themselves were pillars, according to conformation as toward Christ, and according to likeness in grace through Spirit. You will take it then for no other reason than what we just said that Christ has been named a pillar for us; and he was leading when it was day, in a pillar of cloud, and by night, it says, in a pillar of fire, to show them the way. And divine Scripture is accustomed to name night the time before the sojourn, in which, Satan still tyrannizing, the darkness of ignorance was mastering those upon the earth; and day again, the time of our Savior’s sojourn, in which we have been enlightened, receiving into mind the rays of true knowledge of God, and seeing the sun of righteousness with the eyes of the heart; and Paul will testify saying concerning the time before the sojourn

title: Night and day; fire of Law, cloud of baptism; Pharaoh pursues
english: and the one according to it: ‘The night has advanced, and the day has drawn near; let us put away therefore the works of darkness, and put on the weapons of light, that we may walk decently as in day.’ The ancient time therefore being understood unto night, and unto day again the one in which the Only-begotten became human, we say that he was going before those from Israel in a form of fire, as in the law that condemns and chastises (for fire is a sign of chastisement); but of us in a form of cloud, as in a type of holy baptism and of the salvation through water. Or is the cloud not water?
Palladius: How not?

Cyril: And when those from Israel had gone out from the Egyptians’, the one who used to take advantage of old—that is, Pharaoh—was being kindled toward angers, and was attempting to pursue. For ‘He yoked,’ it says, ‘his chariots and took along all his people with himself, and taking six hundred choice chariots, and all the cavalry of the Egyptians, and captains over all.’ And after other things again: ‘And the sons of Israel looking up with their eyes see, and behold the Egyptians had camped behind them, and they feared exceedingly. And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, and were bearing down on Moses openly saying: Because there are no graves in the land of Egypt, have you led us out to kill us in the wilderness? What is this you have done to us, leading us out of Egypt? Was this not the word which we spoke to you in Egypt, saying: Leave us alone that we may serve the Egyptians? For it is better for us to serve Egyptians than to die in this wilderness.’ Toward such things Moses: ‘Take courage,’ he says; ‘stand and see the salvation from the Lord which he will do for us today. For in the manner you have seen Egyptians today, you will not add still to see them unto the age of time. The Lord will war for us, and you will be silent. And the Lord said to Moses: Why do you cry to me? Speak to the sons of Israel, and let them break camp; and you lift up your rod, and stretch out your hand upon the sea, and dry it. And let the sons of Israel go into the midst of the sea according to the dry.’ And God was making clear the manner of the help: for ‘The angel of God who was going before the camp of the sons of Israel removed, and went from behind; and the pillar of the cloud also removed from before their face, and stood from behind them; and it went in between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel, and stood, and there came to be darkness and gloom. And the night passed, and they did not mix with one another the whole night.’ And these things the word of the history weaves for us; but I think we must again see the precision of the thoughts, putting a fine mind into what is written.
Palladius: Very much so.

Cyril: Those from Israel therefore set out hastening unto the holy land, God advancing and leading as in a pillar of fire and of cloud. For there is not, there is not a arriving unto the upper and holy

title: Christ must lead to the city; Red Sea baptism; mediator stands between
english: city, unless Christ is leading, and making clear the road of salvation. And against those who have chosen to do this, the enemies according to this world grind their teeth; yet the law sharpens toward boldness and emboldens those who have feared; and that the throng of the opposed will fall it makes very clear; for the Egyptians’ getting out of the way hints this altogether to us; and those being in fears of suffering God was saving again as in a type of holy baptism. For ‘Speak,’ it says, ‘to the sons of Israel, and let them break camp; and you lift up your rod, and stretch out your hand upon the sea, and dry it; and let the sons of Israel go into the midst of the sea.’ Or does not the divine Paul write concerning the sons of Israel, that all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea?
Palladius: I agree.

Cyril: Those who wish to follow Christ, then, and who hasten toward the city above, must not settle in the law, nor lodge unmoved in the commandments through Moses, and love to dwell in shadows and types; but rather break camp and move over elsewhere—that is, unto holy baptism. For this is what those of old were doing by God’s command, going through the midst of waves, and as Paul says, being baptized in the sea; for then indeed, then they will also have as helper the mediator of God and humans, Christ Jesus. For the Word, being God, became flesh; and in another manner, a mediator economically as one accustomed to go through the middle of both those who worship him and those who pursue them, and not allowing them to mix, and blocking the approaches of the opposed. For ‘The angel of God removed,’ it says, ‘and the pillar of the cloud, and went in between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel, and they did not mix with one another the whole night.’ And again as in an angel and as in a pillar of cloud Christ is signified. For his name is called ‘Angel of great counsel.’
Palladius: With Christ mediating, then, we will not mix with those who wish to war?

Cyril: Thus the matter holds; for you understand rightly. Yet I say that too, and not off the mark, as I think—what seems will go away; for those who have chosen just now to depart from the pleasure-loving and in-world life, and who have been most eager that one must follow the laws of God, yet have not yet been enriched with the grace through holy baptism, are not very strong, or fit toward the need to endure hardship, and to bear toils for virtue, and to be able to carry through an experience of wars. And just as the newly sprouting of plants declines the harm of the sun’s most intense bolt, yet would be injured not moderately if shaken by wilder thrusts of winds, and they altogether need the helps from art, and the surrounding enclosure; in the same way, I think, this

title: Soul before baptism is weak; after the sea Amalek is fought
english: way also the human soul, just now running out from slavery from passions, and shifting harbor toward the better things, and wishing to follow along with the divine law, is tender-minded and more easily touched, and would be easily startled, having seen sweat and war’s law behind, and will think it welcome to pass time again in what it once was. And indeed those from Israel, having seen the Egyptians’ array, and having given up at the mere sight of the war, were attacking the divine Moses saying: ‘Was this not a word which we spoke in Egypt to you saying, Leave us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians? for it is better for us to serve Egyptians than to die in this wilderness.’ Therefore weak unto battle, and most ready toward slavery, and altogether easily terrified before holy baptism is the human soul; but if having obtained the grace it should put on the power from on high, it will most strongly counter those who wish to pursue, and will fight nobly, and would most easily beat off the uprisings of the enemies, Christ generaling and shielding in front. For we will prevail in no other way than according to this very manner.
Palladius: Look then through what examples you will also set this before us; for you will not be at a loss anywhere.

Cyril: Through very many indeed it is easy to show, yet from the first neighbor at least, and from what Moses himself has written; for those who had given up at the mere sight of the Egyptians, when they crossed the Red Sea, and were fulfilling the type of holy baptism (for they were baptized, he says, into Moses, just as also the wise Paul writes, in the cloud and in the sea), were already being shown fight-ready and terrible toward resistance against the enemies—yet through Christ. And it has been written thus: ‘And Amalek came and was warring Israel in Rephidim. And Moses said to Joshua: Choose for yourself powerful men, and going out array against Amalek tomorrow; and behold I have stood upon the top of the hill, and the rod of God is in my hand. And Joshua did just as Moses said to him, and going out arrayed against Amalek; and Moses and Aaron and Hur went up upon the top of the hill. And it came to be, whenever Moses lifted up the hands Israel was prevailing, and whenever he let the hands down Amalek was prevailing. And Moses’ hands were heavy, and taking a stone they put it under him, and he sat upon it, and Aaron and Hur were supporting his hands, from here one and from here one; and Moses’ hands became supported until sun’s settings; and Joshua turned Amalek and all his people in slaughter of sword. And the Lord said to Moses: Write this unto a memorial in a book, and give into Joshua’s ears, that with a wiping I will wipe out the memorial of Amalek from under the heaven. And Moses built an altar to the Lord, and named its name, The Lord my refuge, because with a hidden hand the Lord wars upon Amalek from generations unto generations.’

title: Joshua under Moses; cross-shaped hands defeat Amalek
english: Palladius: And what would the mind of what is written be? for I do not understand very much.

Cyril: And yet, as I think, there is nothing hard for those who wish to see; for having thought of Joshua being ordered by Moses, what else would one suspect than that altogether, that the Word being God came under law, according at least to the schema of the humanity, and was somehow subjected to the commandments through Moses in various ways—here enduring the circumcision according to flesh, here paying the didrachms, and ranging himself with those under law as under law, and saying clearly: ‘I came not to dissolve the law, but to fulfill.’ But even if he came under law because of the human, yet even so he was God, Savior and Redeemer of the whole people. For choosing from the whole people Israel, and from every nation powerful men—I mean again the holy apostles and those called through faith, to whom it would be said well: ‘But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people unto acquisition’—he arrayed with them against the ruler of this age; concerning whom the master of all, himself the one conquering all, says: ‘Now is judgment of this age; now the ruler of this age will be cast outside.’ And the divine John also crowns with a bright vote those who have conquered with him and through him: ‘I write to you,’ he says, ‘young men, that you are strong, and you have conquered the Evil One.’ Or is what I say not true?
Palladius: Very much.

Cyril: And Moses said the arraying must be completed unto tomorrow; for Christ’s achievements did not appear in the time according to him; but they have rather been done in the next and neighboring—that is, after Moses and law. Then Moses goes up toward some hill and upon a crest of a mound, so that he might be able to look down upon the battle and Jesus’ achievements of all in it. For the mystagogy according to law also proportionately leads up toward being able as it were from afar to look upon Christ’s generalships. And when Moses was stretching up the hands, Israel was prevailing; and when letting them down, it was weak, and Amalek was prevailing; for unconquerable to the devil himself and to every enemy, and to the one wishing to ravage bitterly, has become not indeed all Israel, but as many as have honored the conformation toward Christ, through wearing his reproach—that is, the precious cross; for hands shown stretched out into air write clearly the schema of the cross. And as many as did not accept the cross have become easy to overrun for the enemies, not having the helper. When therefore Moses stretches out the hands for us, showing the schema of the cross, and Amalek falls having grown feeble, the schema signifies altogether for us those conquering Satan through the precious cross, and prevailing over the enemies. And when we see him letting the hands down, then Amalek prevailing, those who have come to be under the devil

title: Heavy hands: Israel slow to the cross; altar named the Lord my refuge
english: and conquered we will understand, because of not wishing to accept the cross, to whom also Christ was addressing saying: ‘Amen, amen I say to you, if you do not believe that I am, you will die in your sins.’ And he says Moses’ hands are heavy, and barely being raised, and stretched out very reluctantly, unto the need to show the precious schema of the cross—hinting that enigmatically, I think, that Israel was not very ready unto receiving the faith, coming most reluctantly and barely unto wishing to take up the reproach of Christ; for because of this the divine Paul also names the cross well a scandal to Jews. ‘And taking,’ it says, ‘a stone, they put it under him, and he was sitting upon it, and Aaron and Hur were supporting his hands, from here one and from here one.’ And a precious stone, chosen, cornerstone, honorable is Christ, upon whom also resting (for the sitting makes clear the rest) the more equitable and more teachable of those from Israel, the remnant of the grace according to election, spread the hands—that is, accept the cross—Christ as it were somehow supporting and holding them through even unto this, as is signified in Hur and Aaron, being understood at once as judge and high priest. For Hur was an unbribed judge; and Aaron high priest, the one holding together the remnant according to election of grace of those from Israel, toward the salvation through faith. For this I think is what was said prophetically through Isaiah’s voice: ‘And if the Lord of hosts had not left us a seed, we would have become as Sodom, and we would have been likened as Gomorrah.’ Amalek who stood opposed having fallen therefore—I mean Amalek—‘Write,’ it says, ‘this unto a memorial into a book, and give into Jesus’ ears.’ For through the writing of the holy evangelists Christ’s achievements were going to be stretched unto unfinished and long memory. And it said the writing is to be given into Jesus’ ears. For as it were an offering are praises and encomia to Christ—the writings of the saints. And Amalek already having fallen and been conquered, Moses raises an altar to God; and he also writes a name for it, ‘My Lord, my refuge.’ And this also would be a type of Christ. For he has become Lord to us and refuge; for having conquered the ruler of this age, and having trampled the power of death, and having offered himself for us as it were a blameless victim, unto an odor of fragrance to God and Father. A type of Christ therefore is the altar, for which also a fitting and true name is ‘My Lord, my refuge.’
Palladius: I agree; for you understand rightly.

title: One flock; Jethro comes with Zipporah and the two sons
english: he himself says, having bound the strong one. For the flock that once practiced under that one—I mean those from the nations—he joined to the more ancient flocks; therefore he also was saying: ‘And other sheep I have, which are not from this court, and those too I must lead, and they will hear my voice; and there will come to be one flock, one shepherd.’ And Christ is our peace, according to the Scriptures, the one who made both one, and dissolved the middle wall of the fence, and the enmity in his flesh, abolishing the law of the commandments in decrees, and bringing together into one new human both those from circumcision and those outside law. Observe then again this great mystery, yoked beside what we have just said, as in shadow and enigmas. For ‘Jethro heard,’ it says, ‘the priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-law, all things as many as the Lord did for Israel his own people; for the Lord led Israel out from Egypt. And Jethro Moses’ father-in-law also took Zipporah Moses’ wife after her dismissal, and her two sons; the name of the one Gershom, saying: I was a sojourner in a foreign land; and the name of the second Eliezer, saying: For the God of my father is my helper, and he delivered me from Pharaoh’s hand. And Jethro Moses’ father-in-law came, and the sons and the wife, to Moses into the wilderness, where he had encamped at the mountain of God. And it was announced to Moses saying: Behold your father-in-law Jethro is arriving toward you, and the wife and your two sons with him. And Moses went out unto a meeting with his father-in-law Jethro, and bowed to him, and kissed him, and they greeted one another, and he led them into the tent; and Moses narrated to the father-in-law all things as many as the Lord did to Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for the sake of Israel, and all the toil that came to be for them on the way, and that the Lord delivered them from Pharaoh’s hand, and from the hand of the Egyptians. And Jethro was amazed at all the goods which the Lord did for them, that the Lord delivered them from Egyptians’ hand and from Pharaoh’s hand. And Jethro said: Blessed is the Lord, that he delivered his people from the Egyptians’ hand, and from Pharaoh’s hand. Now I have known that the Lord is great beyond all the gods, because of this, that they set themselves upon them. And Jethro Moses’ father-in-law took whole-burnt-offerings and sacrifices to God; and Aaron and all the elders of Israel arrived to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God. And it came to be after the next day, Moses sat down to judge the people; and all the people were standing by Moses from morning until evening. And Jethro seeing all things as many as he did for the people, says: What is this which you do for the people? Why do you sit alone, and all the people has stood by you from morning until afternoon? And Moses says to the father-in-law: Because the people comes to me to seek a judgment from God. For when there comes to be a dispute for them and they come to me, I judge each, and I set together for them the ordinances of

title: Jethro’s counsel; Midianite as nations coming to the one God
english: God and his law. And Moses’ father-in-law said to him: You are not doing this word rightly; you will not be able to do it alone. And now listen to me, and I will counsel you, and God will be with you. Become you to the people the things toward God, and you will bring up their words toward God, and you will testify to them the ordinances of God and his law, and you will signal to them the ways in which they will walk in them, and the works which they will do. And you look out for yourself from all the people powerful men, he says, and they will judge the people.’ And after other things again: ‘And Moses heard,’ it says, ‘his father-in-law’s voice, and did as many things as he said to him.’
Palladius: Come then again to me, and taking each in part, clarify.

Cyril: Or do you not say the Midianite is foreign-born and from the nations? For he did not spring from Abraham’s root; and he was also otherwise a sacrificer and servant of the will-worship then customarily practiced upon the earth. For they were worshiping, as much account has it, and were thinking among themselves, to a most high God just as indeed also Melchizedek; yet they were also receiving perhaps other gods, numbering with him the exceptional of the creatures—earth and heaven, sun and moon, and the more notable of the stars; and an ancient fault is the corruption and wandering upon this, and it extends even until now and stretches on. For some of those in Phoenicia and Palestine still raving think thus, who name themselves god-fearing, yet walk a middle path of religion, cleaving purely neither to the Jews’ customs nor to the Greeks’, but as it were tossed and divided unto both. And when those from Israel once chose to think thus the prophet Elijah was rebuking saying: ‘Until when will you limp upon both the hams? either Baal, Baal, or to God, God.’ Jethro therefore was also, as is likely, administering some such manner of religion. Who when he knew the things come to be from God toward salvation of those from Israel, being charmed by august and admirable narrations, arrives with all house and all kin toward the holy Moses; who when he saw, received him gladly and has brought him into his own tent. And he narrates more precisely the achievements through the divine strength very well. And the wonder-works beyond every word. For the multitude of those wandering is called unto a change of mind as toward God—I mean the nations—first from hear-sayings which someone might make concerning God, then thus themselves through themselves as it were deserting toward the divine law—that is, the catechesis through holy letter. So that it also runs into the first tent. For the law is introductory; then, having been persuaded by the more ancient narrations, it moves over also unto choosing thereafter to think that God is one and alone, and indeed also unto the need to bear fruit to him. For the Midianite, having heard Moses’ narration, ‘Now I have known,’ he says, that the Lord is great beyond all the gods;
